comment: Masterson is an interesting professor. I really liked how she graded papers, as she let you submit drafts and provided very detailed feedback for you to change things before a final submission. Weekly quizzes on a few news articles which can be tedious if you don't stay on top of them, but overall she's a good professor. I'd take again!

Professor Masterson really cares about her students and gives great feedback on essays. She really wants everyone to succeed and put forth their best effort. Although I struggled a little bit in class at first, I learned a lot. There is a good amount of homework, but Masterson is really flexible and understanding.

Masterson is tough but an exceptional professor. She cares about her students and their work and puts a lot of time into editing. She lets you redo your assignments. She focuses on work ethic and improvement instead of grades. The class is definitely a lot of work, probably one of the more time consuming ones, but totally worth it.

Assignments for Masterson got really long and annoying sometimes. I learned a lot from her and always love listening to her in class, but I'm really annoyed by her grading criteria. She never gives a clear rubric for anything except quizzes. I worked super hard on projects and never got above an A, and a lot of the time she didn't tell me why.

She required us to read 5 washington post articles everyday of the week, and then quizzed us on them (a few relatively easy questions) each week. Other than that, we had a few projects, and I thought she did a good job of assigning different and interesting homework (readings/books, but also movies/videos). Work hard & you'll do well/learn a lot.

I really liked Masterson, although I know some of my classmates didn't. You have to read 6 (interesting except Newton) books in a short amount of time, then after the book take a quiz, and a 500-word essay, and have a graded discussion in class on them. However, the class discussions are fun and she lets you rewrite your papers if you do bad.
